outer_multicall_in_progress.meaning: an outer multicall batch operation is in progress
outer_multicall_in_progress.checkpoint: before the nested inner multicall executes

inner_call_is_nested_multicall.meaning: one inner call of the outer multicall is a delegatecall to multicall itself
inner_call_is_nested_multicall.checkpoint: before the nested inner multicall executes

subsequent_call_requires_fee.meaning: a subsequent call in the outer multicall requires a nonzero fee
subsequent_call_requires_fee.checkpoint: before the nested inner multicall executes

legitimate_batch_completes.meaning: the legitimate fee-requiring batch transaction completes successfully rather than failing
legitimate_batch_completes.checkpoint: after the outer multicall batch executes

core_feature_broken.meaning: the core multicall gas-efficiency/user-experience feature is broken (legitimate fee-requiring batch fails)
core_feature_broken.checkpoint: after the outer multicall batch executes

assumptions: The nested multicall and the subsequent fee-requiring call occur within the same outer multicall transaction.
The attacker can include a nested multicall call in the batch; report does not state an authorization requirement.

unresolved.description: Report does not specify the exact fee amount or the msg.value/msgValue operands used by _checkPayment, so the fee comparison cannot be numerically bound.
Report does not state whether calling multicall requires authorization or whether anyone may call it.

limitations: The impact is formalized as the potential failure of a legitimate fee-requiring batch following a nested multicall; the report's 'potential' modality is preserved by treating the failure as the forbidden outcome under the stated scenario.
The _isMulticall flag reset mechanism is a root cause and is not encoded as a precondition or as the impact itself.
